Social media for hair and beauty salons

Your work is visual and your clients like to see it. Here is what to post through the year, the advertising rules that catch salons out, and how Kanosena can write a week of posts from your own website for you to approve.

Request early access See an example week

Free while we test with our first businesses. Nothing is posted until you approve it.

What’s worth posting

Posts that fill the book and keep clients coming back.

  • Recent work, with permission

    A fresh cut, a colour, a set of nails. Ask the client before you post, and say which service it was.

  • Gaps in the book

    A free slot on Thursday afternoon is worth a quick post. Give the day, the time and how to book.

  • Meet the team

    Introduce each stylist, barber or therapist: what they love doing and which days they work.

  • Aftercare tips

    How to keep a colour bright or make a blow-dry last. Useful posts get saved and shared.

  • Services and prices

    A clear reminder of what you offer and what it costs, kept in line with your website.

  • Gift vouchers

    Ahead of birthdays, Valentine’s Day, Mothering Sunday and Christmas.

Your year at a glance

Moments in the UK calendar worth planning posts around.

January
New year, new look. Quieter weeks are a good time to promote services people have been putting off.
February
Valentine’s Day (14 February): treatments and gift vouchers.
March or April
Mothering Sunday, three weeks before Easter Sunday. Vouchers and treat days.
May to August
Weddings, proms and holidays: bridal trials, summer nails, holiday-ready hair.
September
Back to school and back to routine. Children’s cuts before term starts.
November and December
Party season. Post your December hours early and remind people to book.

Rules worth knowing

Social media posts are advertising, so the usual rules apply. These are the ones that come up most in your line of work.

  • You can’t advertise Botox to the public

    Botox and other anti-wrinkle injections are prescription-only medicines. The Advertising Standards Authority says these may not be advertised to the public, and its warnings have focused on social media. Its guidance explains what you can say about consultations instead.

    Botox: frequently asked questions (ASA)

  • Results photos must be honest

    Don’t use filters or edits that make a treatment look more effective than it is. Adverts, including your own posts, must not mislead.

  • Ask before you post a client

    Get a client’s agreement before you post their photo, even if their face isn’t shown.

  • Prices and offers must be real

    If a post mentions a price or a discount, it should match what clients pay and say when it ends.

General information, checked on 27/11/2026. It isn’t legal advice: check with the body named for your own situation.

How Kanosena helps

You approve. We handle the rest.

  • We read your websiteWe build a short profile of your business, and every fact shows where it came from. You can edit any of it.
  • We write your weekPosts and simple branded graphics in your colours, written only from your profile, with UK dates and seasons in mind.
  • You approve every postApprove, edit, reject or ask for a new version. Only the posts you approve are scheduled.
  • We post and report backApproved posts go out to your Facebook Page, Instagram business account or LinkedIn Page, and we show you how they did.

Questions

Will you mention treatments I don’t offer?

No. Posts are written from your own website and the business profile you check. If a treatment isn’t there, it won’t appear in a post.

Will you use photos of my clients?

No. Each post comes with a simple branded graphic in your colours. If you post photos of clients yourself, get their agreement first.

Can I stop a post at the last minute?

Yes. You can change or cancel a scheduled post at any time before it goes out.
